about: The user stories: what a person sets out to do with Tilo, in their words, and the steps they take. `driver` names the page driver that walks a story as that person; a story with none is listed as not yet automated, and `needs` says what walking it still takes. `stack: false` marks a story walked without a tilo.sh stack of its own. `credentials` marks a story that cannot run without an outside account.

stories.title: Make a workspace, invite someone, and work together live
stories.intent: Ada makes a new workspace and invites Grace. Grace opens the invitation in a browser that has never seen Tilo and joins. Each sees the other in their people list within about two seconds. Grace follows Ada, and what Ada types in a note shows on Grace's screen within about a second.
steps: Ada opens Tilo
Ada opens Tilo again
Ada gives their name
Ada makes a new workspace, “Garden club”
Ada makes an invitation link
Grace opens the invitation in a fresh browser
Grace joins Garden club
Ada and Grace see each other in their people lists
Grace follows Ada
Ada opens Notes and starts a note
Ada types a line in the note
Grace sees Ada’s words

stories.title: See what invited people are doing
stories.intent: A person who invited others sees who is here and what each is working on, follows one of them live, and a mention they write reaches the person it names.
steps: Ada invites Grace and Lin into a workspace
Ada sees who is here and what each is working on
Ada follows Grace and sees Grace's screen live
Ada mentions Lin in Chat
Lin is told of the mention and opens it
stories.needs: A third person on the invite-live driver, and a way to read the mention's notification on Lin's page.

stories.title: Sign up from the wait list and arrive in your own workspace
stories.intent: A stranger at an invitation-only Tilo puts their address on the wait list, confirms it from the mail, is invited, and lands in a workspace of their own.
steps: A stranger opens Tilo and leaves their address on the wait list
They confirm it from the mail
The host invites them from the wait list
They open the invitation mail's link
They arrive in a workspace of their own
stories.needs: The stack's entry set to invitation-only and the mail sink read as onboarding.mjs reads it; that flow's steps recorded through the story recorder.

stories.title: The desktop is easy to use
stories.intent: Someone new to Tilo adds a strip, switches workspaces and finds their settings without being told how.
steps: A newcomer opens their workspace
They add a strip
They switch to another workspace and back
They find their settings
stories.needs: Each step done only through what the screen shows (no search chord a newcomer would not know), so the judge reads whether it was findable.

stories.title: Bring files in and open them
stories.intent: A person brings their files into a workspace by dropping them on the page, through the workspace folder after `tilo login`, and with the `tilo` command, then opens each one.
steps: Ada drops a photo and a PDF on the page
Ada runs `tilo login` and copies a document into the workspace folder
Ada copies a spreadsheet in with the `tilo` command
Ada opens each file in the workspace
stories.needs: A file drop through CDP (Input.dispatchDragEvent), and `tilo login` on the runner with the workspace folder mounted (FUSE in the check's sandbox).

stories.title: Connect an agent over MCP and have it do real work
stories.intent: A person connects their agent to a workspace over MCP. The agent writes a file, adds a Tasks issue, writes a note and posts in Chat, all shown under the agent's name, and when it asks a question the person sees it and answers.
steps: Ada connects their agent to the workspace
The agent writes a file
The agent adds a Tasks issue
The agent writes a note
The agent posts in Chat
Ada sees each change under the agent's name
The agent asks Ada a question, and Ada answers it
stories.needs: A scripted MCP client (the `tilo` MCP server over stdio, as agent-setup.mjs connects one) playing the agent, and a model only where the story is about the agent's own judgment.

stories.title: Connect a mail account with an email and password
stories.intent: A person connects their mail account with only their address and password, then reads, searches and sends mail.
steps: Ada opens Mail and enters their address and password
Mail finds the server by itself and connects
Ada reads the newest mail
Ada searches for an older one
Ada sends a reply, and it arrives
stories.needs: A fake mail provider on the runner (IMAP and SMTP with an autoconfig document at its domain) the stack's Mail can reach.

stories.title: Connect a calendar and create and invite an event
stories.intent: A person connects their calendar, creates an event and invites someone, who receives the invitation.
steps: Ada connects their calendar
Ada creates an event
Ada invites Grace to it
Grace receives the invitation
stories.needs: A CalDAV server on the runner (the Nextcloud container can serve one) and a mail sink to read Grace's invitation.

stories.title: Sign in with Nextcloud and bring files over
stories.intent: A person who keeps their files in Nextcloud signs in with it, and their files sync into or are migrated to their workspace.
steps: Ada chooses Nextcloud and signs in
Ada picks the folders to bring
The files arrive in the workspace
A file changed in Nextcloud changes in the workspace too
stories.needs: A real Nextcloud container (rootless podman on the builder) seeded with a user and files, reachable from the check's sandbox.

stories.title: Sign in with Microsoft for mail and OneDrive
stories.intent: A person signs in with their Microsoft account, and their Outlook mail and OneDrive files show in their workspace.
steps: Ada chooses Microsoft and signs in
Ada's Outlook mail shows in Mail
Ada's OneDrive files show in the workspace
stories.credentials: A Microsoft 365 test tenant with a test user, its OAuth app registration and the user's password as check secrets.
stories.needs: The test tenant's credentials; then the sign-in walked in the browser like any person's.

stories.title: Copy a big folder in, and it is all there everywhere
stories.intent: Ada copies a large folder into their workspace through its mounted folder: a photo library of many small files and a few long videos. The folder lists at once, a second computer joins and shows the workspace in seconds without fetching it all, a photo and a video open there at once, the first computer restarts in seconds, and every file is still there and as copied on both.
steps: Ada copies the folder into their workspace folder
Ada browses the big folder
Ada’s second computer joins and shows the workspace
Ada opens a photo the second computer never fetched
Ada starts a video on the second computer
Ada restarts the first computer
Every file is still there, on both computers
stories.note: Walked on the fs daemons and their mounts (two computers, one joining the other over the network) at one affordable size, set in big-folder.json; the terabyte rungs are the fs-workspace-scale check's.

stories.title: A large workspace stays fast
stories.intent: A workspace with years of files, notes and tasks opens, lists, searches and syncs as fast as an empty one.
steps: Ada opens a workspace with 50,000 files and 10,000 notes
Ada lists a folder of 5,000 files
Ada searches across everything
A change Ada makes reaches their other device
stories.needs: The dataset and steps from the owners of files at scale and of the resource store: a generator and its sizes, and the steps, in large-workspace.json (the driver, large-workspace.mjs, runs each step at every size and reports how its time grew against the workspace's).

stories.title: Notes on the web, page by page
stories.intent: A person opens a workspace's Notes at its own web address, writes a note, sees it persist through a reload, and moves between the list and the note with the browser's back and forward.
steps: Ada opens Notes at its web address
Ada creates a note
Ada types in it
Ada reloads the page, and the note is still there
Ada goes back to the list and forward to the note
stories.needs: The server-rendered Notes pages (/w/<workspace>/notes/<note>) on main; then budgets of first content under 500 ms and an edit shown under 100 ms.
